name: ranked-phrase-search
title: ranked-phrase-search: a zero-dependency CLI that indexes a JSONL corpus and answers term OR exact-phrase queries with the 10 most relevant document ids
interface:
One executable at the project root, `search.mjs` (ES module, zero runtime dependencies, node>=20).
Successor to the deprecated `ranked-search`, which stated the same deliverable without exact-phrase search.
Every command is run from the project root and resolves its index at `./index/` (relative to cwd).

  node search.mjs index <docs.jsonl>
    Reads a JSONL corpus — one {"id","title","body"} object per line — and writes an index
    under ./index/ (created if missing, every previous index file removed first).
    A line that is not valid JSON, or that is not an object with string id/title/body,
    is SKIPPED and counted; indexing still exits 0. Blank lines are not corpus lines
    and are not counted. Exit 0 on success.

  node search.mjs query "<terms>"
    Takes the query as one argument; any further arguments are joined with single
    spaces, so an unquoted multi-word query behaves like the quoted one.
    Prints the ids of the up-to-10 most relevant documents, best first, one id per line,
    nothing else on stdout. Fewer than 10 lines only when fewer documents qualify.
    Relevance ranks title+body against ALL query terms, weighting rare terms more.
    When the query argument contains a double-quoted segment — node search.mjs query '"alpha beta gamma"' —
    that segment is an EXACT PHRASE: only documents in which those tokens (after the project's
    tokenization) occur adjacent and in order, inside the title or inside the body, may be
    printed. The surviving documents are ranked the same way and capped at 10 the same way.
    Several quoted segments must all match; an unterminated quote is not a phrase; a query
    without quotes behaves exactly as it did before phrases existed.
    Exit 0.

  node search.mjs stats
    Prints exactly one JSON object on stdout:
    {"docs": <documents indexed>, "skipped": <malformed lines skipped>, "indexBytes": <total bytes under index/>}
    Exit 0.

Errors — no command, unknown command, wrong argument count, unreadable/missing corpus file,
querying or stat-ing before an index exists — print a human-readable message on stderr,
write nothing to stdout, and exit 1. No command ever leaves a partially written index behind.
nl_description: The whole deliverable of this project: a ranked full-text search command line tool over a flawed JSONL corpus, implemented in plain Node with no dependencies, answering both ordinary term queries and exact-phrase queries. It is judged on five measured dimensions — relevance (mean P@10 over hidden labelled queries, phrase queries included), phrase exactness (a quoted query returns all and only the documents holding that phrase), size (indexBytes / corpus bytes), speed (p95 wall-clock ms per query process) and robustness (indexing a corpus containing malformed lines exits 0 and reports an exact skipped count). Done when every child contract is Done and the end-to-end gate passes: the composed CLI indexes sample-docs.jsonl, answers topic and phrase queries with the right documents, reports exact stats and fails loudly on bad input. Its gate runs the deprecated ranked-search gate too, so nothing that worked before phrases may regress.
